messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@medbridge.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.example.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: No-train commitment + cross-border evidence request

Hi Markus —

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Legal at MedBridge has a couple of gating items before procurement will greenlight a pilot:

- A firm "no-training / no model improvement" commitment for tenant data (including prompts & responses).
- Confirmation of prompt/response ownership and whether outputs are considered customer IP or subject to derivative rights.
- Evidence that data can be kept and processed within the EU (or an EU-resident subprocessor) and details on any cross-border exports.
- A current subprocessor inventory plus the ability to attest on transfers.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can:
1) Add a contractual no-train exhibit and operationally enforce it at the tenant level;
2) Produce a short evidence pack (subprocessor list, flow diagram, residency proof) we can share with our procurement/legal folks.

Timing: procurement would like this by end of week if possible — is that realistic?

Appreciate it —
Sanjay Rao
Head of Security & Compliance
MedBridge Health

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.example.com>

Markus / Lauren —

Quick technical summary and what we can deliver by EOD Thu (3 business days):

1) No-train enforcement
- We can enable a tenant-level "no-learn" flag that prevents any telemetry or prompt/response pairs from entering model improvement pipelines. This is a runtime + configuration switch; we can provide a config screenshot and a short runbook showing where the flag is enforced.

2) Prompt/response ownership
- By default, we treat customer prompts and generated responses as data tied to the customer tenant. Output IP language is legal territory, but operationally we can produce logs that show prompt origin and response timestamps for provenance.

3) Embeddings handling
- Embeddings can be configured to be transient (in-memory only) and not persisted to long-term stores. Where customers request persistence we can mark the objects as non-exportable by default and limit downstream subprocessor access.

4) Residency & exports
- For EU residency we have compute clusters in eu-west-1 and eu-central-1 and can pin a tenant to those regions. We will produce: a) subprocessor inventory CSV; b) export_flow_diagram.png showing all egress/control points; c) a host-level snapshot (redacted) showing S3 bucket region and retention settings.

Attachments we will include in the evidence pack:
- subprocessor_inventory_2027.csv (generated from inventory service)
- export_flow_diagram.png (ops-drawn, simplified)
- config_screenshot.png (tenant config page showing no-learn toggle)

Open questions for legal:
- If we add a DPA exhibit with a no-train clause, do we also need a certified deletion workflow (proof of deletion) for when a customer requests purge? We can implement per-tenant deletion but may need to describe timing.

I'll assemble the artifacts and send a single zip to Markus for review.

- Dev
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Sanjay / Elena —

Thanks for the note and for laying out the procurement checklist. Attached is the initial evidence pack we discussed:

- DPA-exhibit-no-train-draft.pdf (draft exhibit with proposed "no-training" language and output ownership clause)
- subprocessor_inventory_2027.csv (current inventory, includes EU-resident subprocessors highlighted)
- export_flow_diagram.png (simplified architecture showing EU compute zones and egress controls)
- config_screenshot.png (tenant-level no-learn toggle)

Commitments we can make now:
- Operational enforcement of a tenant-level no-train flag; we will prevent tenant data from entering model improvement pipelines and log enforcement events.
- We will provide provenance logs (prompt/response timestamps and request IDs) to support ownership questions.
- We can pin processing to EU regions and provide the subprocessor attestations included in the CSV.

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached DPA exhibit and let us know if your legal team proposes edits. We can accept redlines and iterate — for speed you can mark critical vs. nice-to-have.
2) If the DPA exhibit is acceptable, we can move to a DocuSign flow. I included a placeholder DocuSign link for your convenience.
3) If you need certified deletion proof, flag that now and we'll scope the SLA (we can provide deletion attestations within 5 business days typically).

Happy to hop on a 30-min sync if that helps.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
